text: The collapse of the ancient bridge serves as the inciting incident that disrupts the status quo, forcing the villagers to confront a critical crisis regarding their access to trade and medicine. This event drives the plot forward by compelling the community to shift from dependence on external resources to internal self-reliance. The resulting actions—reconstructing their way of life and finding new paths through the wilderness—develop the narrative by highlighting themes of resilience and ingenuity. Furthermore, the calamity acts as a catalyst for social change, fostering unexpected leadership and uniting the community, which lays the foundation for the development of a more self-sufficient society.
